items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I had a young lady who had gone through all percussion and she was a jazz major on drumset. And part of her master thesis and her recital she had taken and written out and performed her own version of Max Roach’s “Papa Jo”

ctx.x: I’ve got that break down. Before we started I found a little video of you. It looked like you were in a music store and you were playing the hi-hat. Right? And you were showing some things with the — and I said okay I’m going to have Butch Miles come to Hamilton College and all he has to do is bring his hi-hat.

I’d love to. I’d love to. That’s one of the things that I’m — when I teach jazz majors on drumset that’s one of the things that I am a definite dog about, that hi-hat. And I’m so proud to say that two years ago I had a young lady who had gone through all percussion and she was a jazz major on drumset. And part of her master thesis and her recital she had taken and written out and performed her own version of Max Roach’s “Papa Jo” otherwise subtitled “One for Papa” and/or “Mr. Hi-hat.” Nothing but hi-hat, just…
Yeah. What do you tell your, with jazz majors, what do you advise to them as far as post- graduation and making a living?
